meta.title: Every hour has its shade
meta.description: A courtyard kitchen of the Arabian Peninsula that follows the shade from first coffee to midnight — in Al-Balad, Jeddah, and Wadi Hanifah, Riyadh.

hero.intro: Cooking of the Arabian Peninsula in two courtyard houses, Jeddah and Riyadh. The menu follows the sun: bread and coffee by the east wall, the long lunch under the vine, sweets in the long shade, and the whole courtyard at night.
hero.servingNow: What the kitchen is serving now
hero.holdSun: Move across the page to hold the sun

concept.title: In a hot land, a host offers shade before coffee.
concept.body: The old houses of Jeddah and Najd were built around a courtyard, and the day moved around it with the shade. Zill keeps that rhythm. Each part of the day has its own menu, its own light and its own corner of the house — and this page follows the real sun over the house you choose.

day.title: From first bread to the last glass of tea

dawn.title: Dawn
dawn.body: The tannour is lit in the dark. By the time the call to prayer ends, the first tamees is cooling on the east wall.

morning.title: Morning shade
morning.body: Families at the long table, foul in clay pots, eggs from the east wall, and coffee pale with cardamom.

noon.title: The short shade
noon.body: The sun stands overhead and the shade draws in under the vine. Lunch is long, shared and unhurried.

afternoon.title: The long shade
afternoon.body: Shadows stretch across the floor. Pour-over at the bar, luqaimat fried to order, a sweet to share.

dusk.title: Maghrib
dusk.body: The plaster turns violet. Lamps are lit one by one, the ember grill wakes, the courtyard fills.

night.title: Night
night.body: The whole courtyard, open to the sky: ember-grilled fish, the Sundial tasting menu, mint tea at midnight.

signature.title: Served now at {house}
signature.body: A few plates from the menu being served at this moment. The full menu opens on the same hour.
signature.nothing: The kitchen is resting. These are the plates it wakes up to.

room.title: Two courtyards, one clock, two suns
room.body: A coral-stone house in Al-Balad, Jeddah, and a mud-brick courtyard on the edge of the palm groves of Wadi Hanifah. Both keep Riyadh time, but not the same sun: Jeddah's sunset comes some twenty minutes later.

chef.quote: We cook what the hour asks for. Bread at dawn, nothing heavy at noon, the ember grill when the air cools.
